content:
US immigration officers detained a Chinese-born doctoral student at Princeton University at a Washington airport on Thursday, hours after she presented her research at one of the world's largest neuroscience conferences, in a case that has drawn protests from scientists and an emergency intervention by a federal judge.

Eva Yi Xie, 24, a third-year PhD candidate at the Princeton Neuroscience Institute, was taken into custody by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) on 19 November at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Arlington, Virginia, as she prepared to board a domestic flight home to New Jersey, according to the South China Morning Post, which confirmed the detention, and her laboratory.

Xie had been in Washington for the Society for Neuroscience's annual meeting, where she presented a research poster on decision-making neural circuits. The conference, the field's premier annual gathering, ended on 18 November and drew more than 20,000 registrations from academia and industry.

According to her lab, the Brody Lab, Xie sent a call for help to her lab mates on Slack on 19 November and then lost contact. An ICE detainee search returned a record for a Yi Xie, born in China, listed as in custody, without specifying where she was being held. The Brody Lab said she was being held at an ICE facility in Chantilly, Virginia. She remained in custody on Friday, the Washington Post reported, citing university officials.

Xie is described by colleagues and her faculty adviser as a gifted and productive researcher. She attended the Bronx High School of Science in New York and graduated from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 2024 with a double major in computer science and mathematics, according to The Tech, MIT's student newspaper.

Her immigration history is at the centre of the case. Xie came to the United States legally from Shanghai in 2016 as a minor, as a high-school student dependent, and her family filed an affirmative asylum application with US Citizenship and Immigration Services within a year of arrival, according to her lawyer, Kerry Doyle. The asylum claim is still pending, with an immigration court hearing set for January 2028.

The Department of Homeland Security has given a different account of her status. The department stated that Xie, a Chinese national, was admitted to the United States temporarily in 2016 and was required to leave by September of that year, a position that treats her continued presence as an overstay. Neither the department nor ICE has publicly explained why she was detained at the airport this week rather than at any earlier point.

Her lawyers have challenged the arrest in federal court, filing an emergency habeas corpus petition asking a judge to determine the legality of her detention. A federal judge has ordered ICE not to transfer Xie out of the Eastern District of Virginia while the petition is being considered, according to the Daily Princetonian, Princeton's student-run newspaper.

Members of the scientific community and Princeton professors have criticised the arrest and called for her release. US Senator Andy Kim, a Democrat from New Jersey, confirmed to other media outlets that his office is working to secure Xie's release.

The detention has also heightened concern among international scholars about travelling within the United States for academic conferences, according to CASRAI, a research-information organisation that has followed the case. Xie was detained on a domestic flight, not at an international border, after attending a routine academic meeting — a detail that has alarmed researchers who travel regularly between US universities and conferences.

For now, the case turns on two parallel tracks: the habeas corpus proceedings in federal court, which will test whether the detention itself was lawful, and the long-pending asylum claim, which is not due to be heard by an immigration court until January 2028. Until a judge rules, Xie remains in ICE custody in Virginia, and her laboratory says it has had no contact with her since her message on 19 November.

The photograph accompanying this article shows Nassau Hall, Princeton University's administration building. summary: US immigration officers detained Eva Yi Xie, a 24-year-old Princeton neuroscience PhD student, at a Washington airport on 19 November after she presented research at a major conference. Her asylum claim has been pending since 2016, and a federal judge has blocked ICE from transferring her while her lawyers challenge the arrest.
title: ICE detains Princeton PhD student Eva Yi Xie at Washington airport after neuroscience conference
